{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVaC1p88AAAABalz3Wg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BpEKozhEMVok", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BpEKo", "number": 12, "title": "Support multi-file RTL projects and top-module selection in the browser", "body": "## Problem

WebRTL's browser compiler already accepts a project with `{ files, top }`, but the published editor hardcodes a single `counter.v` file and top module `counter`. That prevents using normal multi-module RTL projects and is an immediate blocker for an eventual **SNES hardware demo inside WebRTL** (CPU, PPU, APU, memory, etc.).

Before integrating a 65C816 CPU core, make the browser able to load and compile a small multi-file Verilog project. This should remain a generic WebRTL capability, not a SNES-specific workflow.

## Expected outcome

A user can manage multiple Verilog source files in the browser, select the top module, compile the whole project **entirely client-side**, and run the resulting simulation.

Keep the first demonstration small: a top-level counter whose logic is split across at least two separate `.v` files. Editing a helper module and recompiling must change the output of the actual generated WASM circuit.

## Scope

- Provide a minimal project/file UI: add or import multiple local `.v` files, select the file to edit, rename/remove files, and specify the top-module name.
- Pass the complete file map and chosen top module to the **existing** browser `compileProject({files, top})` pipeline. Reuse its virtual filesystem and diagnostics rather than introducing another compiler.
- Build/run the split-module example using the existing Run / Pause / Step / Reset controls.
- Show understandable errors for missing top modules, invalid source names, conflicting/duplicate filenames, and compilation errors, without losing the current project unnecessarily.
- Keep the existing single-file counter example functional.
- Document supported filenames, top-module selection, size limits, and current constraints.

### Important boundary

The simulator's current board adapter still expects `clk`, `reset`, and 8-bit `count`. **This Issue does not generalize arbitrary top-level I/O yet**; the multi-file example should preserve that interface. Supporting a 65C816 CPU's buses/register outputs and ROM/RAM loading is a follow-up task.

## Out of scope

- Implementing or integrating the SNES CPU/PPU/APU in this PR.
- VHDL support, arbitrary include trees/third-party build systems, pin mapping, or physical FPGA deployment.
- A full IDE, syntax server, persistent workspaces, Git integration, or complete directory/project import.
- Changing the video/audio output feature being developed in #10 / PR #11, except where compatibility is necessary.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] A user can create or import at least two separate `.v` source files, switch between them, and edit each file without losing its changes.
- [ ] The top module can be selected or entered in the UI and is used by the actual browser compiler instead of being hardcoded to `counter`.
- [ ] A provided two-file RTL example compiles on a static site under `/webrtl/` and runs in WASM; changing a helper module changes the observable counter behavior after recompilation.
- [ ] Run / Pause / Step / Reset and the existing single-file counter example continue to work.
- [ ] Invalid filenames, missing top modules, duplicate names and invalid Verilog yield actionable errors; the user can fix and recompile.
- [ ] Real browser tests exercise multi-file compilation and edited-source behavior, plus single-file regression, with no remote compilation API.
- [ ] README explains the new workflow and remaining I/O/HDL constraints.
- [ ] Avoid introducing a general IDE framework or unrelated SNES implementation as part of this small prerequisite.

## Optional validation

- Import more than two files and measure compilation time and memory usage.
- Try a candidate open-source 65C816 core to catalog unsupported HDL constructs and licensing, without requiring the core to work in this Issue.

## Required post-merge verification

After deployment, check the public GitHub Pages site can compile the two-file example and run it. Record the result separately; this is not a pre-merge condition.

## Follow-up direction toward the SNES demo

1. Add a CPU-oriented RTL host interface and a minimal ROM/RAM test harness.
2. Compile and run a real 65C816 core with a tiny permitted test program; verify PC/register/memory changes against known results.
3. Extend toward video/PPU, audio/APU, and inputs using reusable WebRTL interfaces, then investigate real-time performance.

SNES should be a demonstration **inside the WebRTL repository**, while WebRTL itself remains a general-purpose RTL simulator.

## Related issues

- #3 — Project vision
- #8 — Browser-side Verilog compilation (completed)
- #10 — Video/audio outputs (separate work)
